title: db-domain-publishes-a-client-tool
intention: db_domain publishes its socket client as a tool nested in the device — cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/, charter published_by_device true, public_interface the one module cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store — and every caller in the repo imports that module, so nothing reaches into db_domain's own code and db_domain can change everything underneath.
why: RULE 1 agreed detail (2): the db_domain exception becomes a published client tool everyone imports, so db_domain can change underneath without breaking a caller
traces_to: RULE 1 agreed detail (2) (Akien, 2026-10-01): 'there should still be a public interface everyone uses, so we can change things about the db underneath' — the client talks straight to the db over its socket, no bus hop, for graph-tree traffic volume; Law 6 (db_domain owns the client and gates its writes); parent 8e3474a6ae43.
how: Measured 2026-10-02 (encapsulation_breaches over the live repo): 48 into_device rows target cairn/devices/db_domain, every one through the single module cairn.devices.db_domain.store (6 code + 42 instrument sites across librarian 14, inference_domain 12, bus 6, build_inspector 2, tools/orient 2, tools/tree 2, seven codemother machines 1 each, tester 1, skill_block 1, skills/moreabout 1); a grep for 'db_domain.store' or 'db_domain import store' finds 47 .py files including db_domain's own, plus bin/cmd/probescan line 294. Callers use nearly the whole surface (read 100, scratch 47, connect 46, write 30, update 20, create_owned_table 18, owner_of 16, ...), so the whole of store.py is the client: git mv cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py to cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py (history kept), add __init__.py files, write the client's charter through the artifact door, and rewrite every import line to `from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client import store` (the local name `store` is unchanged, so no call site moves). The sole-path sieve's `only` is the prefix cairn/devices/db_domain/, which the nested tool stays inside. db_domain's own charter `invoke` names the client module. The proof is cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py, written red first.
falsifier: RED if: (1) the live encapsulation_breaches carries any row whose target is cairn/devices/db_domain; (2) any file imports cairn.devices.db_domain.store, the old file cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py exists, or a charter's invoke still names the old import; (3) the client charter does not declare published_by_device true with public_interface exactly ['cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store'], or that module does not expose connect, read, write, update, query, delete, create_owned_table, owner_of and scratch. WRONG INTENT if a caller needs a name the client does not publish. Horizon: the tester seal of cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py.
watchme: none, because the encapsulation_holds sieve (ticket 56d1aff4455e, proof cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_encapsulation_holds.py) reads the live repo on every inspector run; a reach back into db_domain reds there the moment it is written, so there is no runtime behaviour left for a probe to watch
children: none, because the edits are one git mv, one new charter, one proof, and a one-line import rewrite in each of the 47 importing files plus bin/cmd/probescan
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Which files? every .py whose import line is `from cairn.devices.db_domain import store` (with or without `as _store`, noqa, trailing comment) or `from cairn.devices.db_domain.store import OwnershipError`, plus bin/cmd/probescan:294 — replace only the dotted path, keep the alias and the trailing comment. (2) The move? `git mv cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py`, empty __init__.py in tools/ and tools/client/. (3) The charter? cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/intention+why.json through cairn artifact write --verb charter: what/why naming detail (2), published_by_device true, public_interface ['cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store'], owner db_domain. (4) Proof? three teeth, one per falsifier clause, resolving the client late.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient cfdb03d2ffc9 .. validate c7733464393f, each learned)

decisions.text: STEP 1 — the proof, already written red at cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py (do not rewrite it). Its three teeth, PROVES keys 1/2/3: (1) nothing_reaches_into_db_domain — no row of cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector.encapsulation_breaches(repo) has target 'cairn/devices/db_domain'; (2) the_old_door_is_gone — no file in cairn.tools.import_sieve.sieve.import_graph(repo) imports cairn.devices.db_domain.store, cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py does not exist, and no charter's invoke contains 'db_domain import store' without the client path; (3) the_client_is_published — the client charter has published_by_device true and public_interface exactly ['cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store'], and that module exposes connect, read, write, update, query, delete, create_owned_table, owner_of, scratch. Red now: 0/3.

STEP 2 — the move: mkdir -p cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client; create empty cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/__init__.py and cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/__init__.py; git mv cairn/devices/db_domain/store.py cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py. store.py reads no path off __file__ (grep finds none), so its bytes move unchanged.

STEP 3 — the import rewrite, in every .py file in the repo (excluding .git, cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_encapsulation_holds.py whose mentions are fixture strings, and the proof itself) plus bin/cmd/probescan: replace 'from cairn.devices.db_domain import store' with 'from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client import store' and 'from cairn.devices.db_domain.store import' with 'from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store import'. Only the dotted path changes; aliases (as _store), noqa markers and trailing comments stay. The local name store is unchanged, so no call site moves. Then grep for the old dotted path returns nothing outside the two excluded files.

STEP 4 — the charters, both through cairn artifact write <abs path> --verb charter --why '4cbf6e28126e ...' --from <file>. (a) NEW cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/intention+why.json, a tool charter: component 'client', runtime_role/node_class 'tool', published_by_device true, public_interface ['cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store'], what (the socket client: connect/read/write/update/query/delete/create_owned_table/owner_of/scratch over the owner-gated store; every caller uses only this module of db_domain), why (RULE 1 detail (2) quoted; 48 reaches measured before; straight to the socket, no bus hop, for graph-tree volume), entry (GRAFTED by git mv), invoke, state_and_history (a tool holds no state of its own, Law 6), proof, gates (encapsulation_holds admits reaches only through this tool), falsifier, learns and how_it_learns (one answer, the same text: it does not; fixed floor), traces_to, owner (none — a tool has users), gated_by ['CC']. (b) db_domain's own charter: invoke's import becomes '`from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client import store`', the rest of invoke unchanged; public_interface stays [] (a device's interface is the bus plus the client tool).

STEP 5 — verify and seal: python3 cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py exits 0 (3/3); cairn test cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py --netns --seal seals it into cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/validations/; the commit's reseal door reproves every standing proof whose sealed inputs named the moved store.py; then cairn test --hollow 4cbf6e28126e --seal.
ADDENDUM to D1 — yes: the proof is committed in the repo before BUILDME (commit f2fb7bc1) and already reads 0/3. The builder creates and edits nothing in it.

ADDENDUM to D4 — the template is cairn/tools/bus_client/intention+why.json (a tool charter): same keys. --from takes a JSON file holding the WHOLE new charter, written by the builder to a scratch path and passed as --from <that file>; the door writes it byte for byte. Explicit values for the client charter: invoke = '`from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client import store` (and `from cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store import OwnershipError`). Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py` (exit 0 = green).'; proof = 'proofs/test_client.py — three teeth, one per falsifier clause of 4cbf6e28126e'; traces_to = ['RULE 1 (a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes)', 'Law 6 (one owner per table; the owner CHECK lives in this module)', 'Law 4 (the owner gate is a schema CHECK)']; falsifier = 'Red if any import outside db_domain lands on db_domain code other than cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client.store, if anything imports cairn.devices.db_domain.store, or if this charter stops declaring published_by_device and exactly its one module.'; gates = 'encapsulation_holds in build_inspector admits a reach into db_domain only through this tool; the tester seals proofs/test_client.py into validations/.' For db_domain's own charter edit, --from is a copy of its current charter with only the invoke import changed.

ADDENDUM to D5 — the sequence: (a) run the proof, 3/3 green; (b) git add -A the moved, new and rewritten files and git commit -m '4cbf6e28126e: db_domain publishes its client tool; every caller imports it'. The pre-commit hook runs the reseal door AUTOMATICALLY — it reproves every standing proof whose sealed inputs include a staged file and fails the commit if one reds; nothing is invoked by hand. (c) cairn test cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_client.py --netns --seal --timeout 900, then commit the new validation. (d) cairn test --hollow 4cbf6e28126e --seal --timeout 900 — it reverts each build file to the BUILDME commit in a throwaway worktree and checks a declared tooth reds; commit its evidence.

THE TOOL CHARTER'S KEY SET, complete — exactly these keys and no others (no filed_edges, no claim_provenance, no provenance: those are device-history keys, not required by any sieve for a tool): component, runtime_role ("tool"), role ("charter"), schema_version ("v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands"), node_class ("tool"), node_class_role, public_interface, what, why, entry, invoke, state_and_history, proof, gates, falsifier, learns, how_it_learns (same text as learns), traces_to (list of str), owner, gated_by (["CC"]). The db_domain client adds published_by_device (true); the scratch tool does not. Every value is given in the D4 step and its addendum, which together are the one D4; the builder needs no file beyond the ticket, though cairn/tools/bus_client/intention+why.json shows the same shape.
ADDENDUM to D4 — node_class_role = "domain client" (the exact string). It is not auto-filled by any door; the builder writes it into the charter JSON with the other keys.
